_doc: The shape `npm run import:crowdfunding` reads. Copy this to scripts/crowdfunding-scan.json (the default filename, gitignored) and replace the contents with a real scan. Full field reference: docs/info/crowdfunding-and-accessories.md.
_warning: ⚠️ The two `books` entries below are ONE novel delivered twice — a deluxe hardcover and an EPUB — by ONE pledge. That is the shape a Kickstarter actually has, and it is the thing that must not be collapsed into a single line. Two rows, one work, and the audit prints `2 lines across 1 book`.
_accounts: ⚠️ `account` is required on every pledge. There are TWO BackerKit logins and a pledge that does not say which one cannot be reconciled against a scan of either.
_notCreated: ⚠️ The importer creates no `work` and no `edition` rows. A book not already in the catalog is reported and skipped; a reward with no matching printing lands with edition_id NULL and the audit counts it. Both are deliberate — see the script header.
_notCrowdfunding: ⚠️ Barnes & Noble does NOT belong in this file. It is a shop, and a shop purchase already has a home: `copy.vendor`, `copy.acquired_on`, `copy.price_paid_cents`. The test is whether the money bought a promise or a product.
_signed: ⚠️ Signed/numbered is never a field — it is prose in the reward title ("Book 1 will be Signed & Numbered", "CONQUEROR -- SIGNED PAPERBACK+", "Legendary Book Box (Uniquely Numbered)"). The importer prints a prompt; a person ticks `copy.is_signed` and writes `edition.edition_name`.

campaigns.name: Dungeon Crawler Carl: The Butcher's Masquerade
campaigns.creator: Matt Dinniman

books._why: MEASURED: one pledge routinely delivers ebook + print + AUDIOBOOK together (Space Knight 5 and 6, Tamer Bk 11, Fires of December). ⚠️ `editionVerdict: "none"` is required on an audiobook line — EDITION_FORMATS has no audiobook value and never will, so without it this row sits in the audit's `no printing` queue forever.
books.title: The Butcher's Masquerade

accessories.name: Desktop wallpaper pack
accessories.notes: ⚠️ digital, so it is a reward but not a thing on a shelf

pledges._why: The same campaign, backed again from the second BackerKit login. Two pledges, not one — and the campaign's audit counts the work ONCE across both.

campaigns._why: A pledge whose reward line names both a hardcover and an ebook in one string. The audit reports it as `needs splitting` rather than guessing — see pledgeItemMedium in packages/core/src/crowdfunding.ts.
campaigns.name: An Example Indiegogo Book
campaigns.creator: Some Publisher

books.title: An Example Indiegogo Book
books.notes: one line, two things — split it into two once the editions exist

books._why: MEASURED: a single reward line can cover SEVERAL works — "Collector's Edition Trilogy" is three books. They are N rows sharing one `externalRef` and one `title`; that is what groups them, and migration 0010's external-ref index includes work_id so all three land instead of only the first. Also note the signed prose: rewardFlags() reads it and the importer prints a prompt, but nothing writes copy.is_signed — a person ticks it.
books.title: Collector's Edition Trilogy
books.notes: row 1 of 3 for one reward line — repeat with the other two titles

accessories._why: ⚠️ This pledge has TWO distinct books, so the importer refuses to guess and requires `title`+`authors` (or `workId`) on every accessory. With exactly one book it would attach automatically.
accessories.name: Signed bookplate
accessories.title: An Example Indiegogo Book

accessories._why: MEASURED: high-value pledges are overwhelmingly accessories — the Primal Hunter box set is ONE book product and roughly TWENTY-THREE pins, standees, plushies, bookmarks and a slipcase.
accessories.name: Guild standee set
accessories.title: An Example Indiegogo Book

accessories._why: MEASURED: some accessories are DIGITAL — an STL file, a concept-art PDF. Never assume an accessory is a thing on a shelf.
accessories.name: Dragon STL file
accessories.title: An Example Indiegogo Book

accessories._why: MEASURED: "V2 or V3 Bundle w/ V1 Jacket" — a dust jacket delivered by THIS campaign for a book bought in an EARLIER one. Set `copyId` in the app afterwards; the accessory belongs to a copy that predates the pledge that sent it, which is why copy_id and pledge_id are separate columns.
accessories.name: V1 dust jacket
accessories.title: An Example Indiegogo Book
